title: Reported speech: dice que, dijo que
summary: Pass on what people say and ask: dice que, dijo que, preguntó si, me pide que.
focus: Reporting statements, questions and requests, with the tense, person, time and place shifts
content:
## Dice que: same tense, new speaker

To pass on what someone says, use **decir que** + their sentence. With a reporting verb in the present (**dice**, **cuenta**, **explica**) the tense stays. Only the person shifts, so **yo** becomes **él / ella** and **mi** becomes **su**.

- Ana: «Estoy cansada.» → **Ana dice que está cansada.** (Ana says she's tired.)
- Leo: «Mi coche no funciona.» → **Leo dice que su coche no funciona.** (Leo says his car doesn't work.)

Other reporting verbs: **contar** (to tell), **explicar** (to explain), **comentar** (to mention), **asegurar** (to assure), **contestar** (to answer). A message passed on is **un recado**. English can drop *that*; Spanish never drops **que**.

## Dijo que: the tense steps back

When the reporting verb is in the past (**dijo**, **contó**, **explicó**), the verb inside usually steps back:

| they said | you report |
|---|---|
| present: «Estoy en casa.» | imperfect: **dijo que estaba en casa** |
| future: «Vendré.» | conditional: **dijo que vendría** |
| ir a: «Voy a salir.» | **dijo que iba a salir** |
| preterite: «Fui al cine.» | stays: **dijo que fue al cine** |
| imperfect, conditional | stay as they are |

If it is still true now, the present may stay: **me dijo que tiene dos hijos**. A further step back for the preterite is coming at B2.

## Time and place move too

Reported later or somewhere else, words of time and place move with the story:

| they said | you report |
|---|---|
| **hoy** | **ese día** |
| **mañana** | **al día siguiente** |
| **ayer** | **el día anterior** |
| **aquí** | **allí** |
| **este / esta** | **ese / esa** |

- Carlos: «Mañana trabajo aquí.» → **Carlos dijo que al día siguiente trabajaba allí.** (Carlos said he was working there the next day.)

Only shift what has really changed: reported the same evening, **mañana** is still **mañana**.

## Questions and requests

A yes/no question is reported with **preguntar si** (*whether*, no accent). A question word stays, **accent included**:

- «¿Tienes hambre?» → **Me pregunta si tengo hambre.**
- «¿Dónde vives?» → **Me preguntó dónde vivía.**
- «¿Cuándo llegas?» → **Me preguntó cuándo llegaba.**

An order or request is reported with **decir que** or **pedir que** + present subjunctive after a present verb:

- «Ven a casa.» → **Mamá me dice que venga a casa.** (Mum tells me to come home.)
- «Esperadme.» → **Os pide que la esperéis.** (She's asking you to wait for her.)

Reporting a request after **dijo** needs a new tense, which comes at B2.

vocabulary.example: Mi hermana dice que la película es muy buena.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My sister says the film is very good.

vocabulary.example: Pedro nos contó que su abuelo era pescador.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Pedro told us his grandfather was a fisherman.

vocabulary.example: La profesora explicó que el examen sería en junio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The teacher explained that the exam would be in June.

vocabulary.example: Elena comentó que el restaurante estaba cerrado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Elena mentioned that the restaurant was closed.

vocabulary.example: El mecánico me aseguró que el coche estaría listo el viernes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mechanic assured me the car would be ready on Friday.

vocabulary.example: Le pregunté por la fiesta y contestó que no podía ir.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I asked her about the party and she answered that she couldn't go.

vocabulary.example: Te dejo un recado: Juan dice que llega tarde.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here's a message for you: Juan says he's running late.

vocabulary.example: Mi vecino me preguntó si necesitaba ayuda.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My neighbour asked me whether I needed help.

vocabulary.example: El camarero nos pide que esperemos un momento.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The waiter is asking us to wait a moment.

vocabulary.example: Nos explicó que ese día no trabajaba.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He explained to us that he wasn't working that day.

vocabulary.example: Prometió que volvería al día siguiente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She promised she would come back the next day.

vocabulary.example: Me contó que el día anterior llovió mucho.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He told me it had rained a lot the day before.

vocabulary.example: Dijo que vivía allí desde pequeño.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He said he had lived there since he was little.

quiz.prompt: Marta: «Estoy cansada.» → Marta dice que ___ cansada.
quiz.explanation: With dice que (present) the tense stays the same; only the person shifts from yo to ella, giving está.
hints: A present reporting verb keeps the same tense.
Who is tired now: yo or ella?

quiz.prompt: Ayer Marta dijo: «Estoy cansada.» → Marta dijo que ___ cansada.
quiz.explanation: After a past reporting verb (dijo) the present steps back to the imperfect, so estoy becomes estaba.
hints: Dijo is in the past, so the present steps back one tense.

quiz.prompt: Luis: «Iré a la fiesta.» → Luis dijo que ___ (ir) a la fiesta, pero al final no fue.
quiz.explanation: After dijo que the future becomes the conditional, so iré becomes iría.
hints: After dijo que, the future becomes the conditional.
Ir is regular in the conditional, so add -ía to the infinitive.

quiz.prompt: Pablo: «Ayer perdí las llaves.» → Pablo me contó que ___ las llaves el día anterior.
quiz.explanation: In everyday speech a preterite stays a preterite and only the person changes, so perdí becomes perdió. The careful written form, the pluperfect (había perdido), comes at B2. Ayer becomes el día anterior.
hints: What happens to the preterite after contó que?

quiz.prompt: Hace un mes, Lucía me dijo: «Te llamaré mañana.» → Lucía me dijo que me llamaría ___.
quiz.explanation: A month later, her 'tomorrow' is long gone: mañana becomes al día siguiente.
hints: Is her 'mañana' still tomorrow today?

quiz.prompt: Ana: «¿Tienes hambre?» → Ana me pregunta ___ tengo hambre.
quiz.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with preguntar si (whether), and this si has no accent.
hints: A yes/no question has no question word to keep.
The word for 'whether', with no accent.

quiz.prompt: El profesor: «¿Dónde vivís?» → El profesor nos preguntó ___ vivíamos.
quiz.explanation: A reported question keeps its question word and its accent: preguntó dónde vivíamos.
hints: The question word stays, and so does its accent.

quiz.prompt: Mi madre: «Llama a tu abuela.» → Mi madre me dice que ___ (llamar) a mi abuela.
quiz.explanation: An order reported with dice que takes the present subjunctive: me dice que llame. Tu abuela becomes mi abuela.
hints: An order, not a fact, so use the subjunctive.
-ar verbs take -e in the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Mi jefe: «Te lo prometo: el informe está bien.» → Mi jefe me ___ que el informe estaba bien.
quiz.explanation: Asegurar means to assure, and the boss insists it's fine. Preguntar would need si, pedir would need the subjunctive.
hints: He promises, so which verb means to assure?

conversations.title: The landlady called
conversations.scenario: Irene took a call from their landlady yesterday and passes the message on to her flatmate Dani.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Dani, ayer llamó la casera mientras estabas en el trabajo.
lines.meaning: Dani, the landlady called yesterday while you were at work.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Ah, sí? ¿Y qué te dijo?
lines.meaning: Oh really? And what did she tell you?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Me dijo que el lunes venía el fontanero a arreglar la ducha.
lines.meaning: She told me the plumber was coming on Monday to fix the shower.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Por fin! ¿Te preguntó si estaríamos en casa?
lines.meaning: At last! Did she ask you whether we'd be at home?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí. Le contesté que yo estaría allí toda la mañana.
lines.meaning: Yes. I answered that I'd be there all morning.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Genial. ¿Y comentó algo del alquiler?
lines.meaning: Great. And did she mention anything about the rent?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, explicó que el año que viene el alquiler subiría un poco.
lines.meaning: Yes, she explained that the rent would go up a bit next year.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Cuánto? ¡Siempre nos asegura que es un piso barato!
lines.meaning: How much? She always assures us it's a cheap flat!

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: No lo sé. Dice que la llames tú esta tarde.
lines.meaning: I don't know. She says you should call her this afternoon.
lines.note: An order reported with dice que: present subjunctive.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Vale, la llamo después de comer. ¿Algo más?
lines.meaning: OK, I'll call her after lunch. Anything else?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí: dice que el fontanero es muy puntual, así que no te quedes dormido.
lines.meaning: Yes: she says the plumber is very punctual, so don't oversleep.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Oye, eso lo dice por mí!
lines.meaning: Hey, she's saying that because of me!

listening.text: Dice que tiene mucho sueño.
listening.meaning: He says he's very sleepy.

listening.text: Mi primo dijo que tenía hambre.
listening.meaning: My cousin said he was hungry.
listening.note: Tengo becomes tenía after dijo que.

listening.text: Nos contó que el ascensor no funcionaba.
listening.meaning: She told us the lift wasn't working.
listening.note: New word: el ascensor = the lift.

listening.text: Mi jefa siempre me pide que llegue temprano.
listening.meaning: My boss always asks me to arrive early.

listening.text: Carmen comentó que ese día perdió el autobús.
listening.meaning: Carmen mentioned that she missed the bus that day.

listening.text: El médico me explicó que la herida era pequeña.
listening.meaning: The doctor explained to me that the wound was small.
listening.note: New word: la herida = the wound.

listening.text: Ayer Pablo me aseguró que vendría a la cena.
listening.meaning: Yesterday Pablo assured me he would come to dinner.
listening.note: Vendré becomes vendría after a past verb.

listening.text: Los vecinos nos contaron que iban a pintar la escalera al día siguiente.
listening.meaning: The neighbours told us they were going to paint the staircase the next day.
listening.note: New word: la escalera = the staircase.

guide.tip: Ask two things: is the reporting verb past (dijo) or present (dice)? And is it still today, here, for the same person?

bites.title: Dice que: same tense
bites.rule: With a present reporting verb (dice, cuenta, explica) the tense stays. Only the person shifts, for example yo to él and mi to su.
bites.example: Leo dice que su coche no funciona.
bites.example_meaning: Leo says his car doesn't work.

bites.title: Dijo que: step back
bites.rule: After a past verb, the present becomes the imperfect (estoy, estaba) and the future becomes the conditional (vendré, vendría). The preterite stays a preterite (fui, fue).
bites.example: Dijo que vendría y que estaba cansado.
bites.example_meaning: He said he would come and that he was tired.

bites.title: Time and place move
bites.rule: Reported later or elsewhere, hoy becomes ese día, mañana becomes al día siguiente, ayer becomes el día anterior and aquí becomes allí.
bites.example: Dijo que al día siguiente trabajaba allí.
bites.example_meaning: He said he was working there the next day.

bites.title: Questions and requests
bites.rule: Yes/no questions: preguntar si. Question words keep their accent (dónde, cuándo). Orders: dice que + present subjunctive.
bites.example: Me pregunta dónde vivo y me dice que vaya.
bites.example_meaning: She asks me where I live and tells me to go.

sorts.title: After dijo que, the verb becomes…
sorts.why: The present becomes the imperfect, the future becomes the conditional and the preterite stays.

sorts.title: A report or an order?
sorts.why: Passing on a fact takes the indicative; telling someone to do something takes the present subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Ayer Luis dijo que vendrá a la fiesta, pero no vino.
spots.why: After dijo que the future becomes the conditional.
A reported question keeps the accent of its question word.

spots.sentence: Ana me pregunta sí tengo hambre.
Mi madre me pide que llamo a la abuela.
Hace un mes Lucía dijo que me llamaría mañana.
spots.why: A month later, her 'tomorrow' is al día siguiente.

builds.text: Me dijo que tenía mucho trabajo.
builds.meaning: She told me she had a lot of work.

builds.text: Nos aseguró que lo haría al día siguiente.
builds.meaning: He assured us he would do it the next day.

builds.text: Ana dice que su hermano vive allí.
builds.meaning: Ana says her brother lives there.

builds.text: Le pregunté dónde vivía su hermana.
builds.meaning: I asked him where his sister lived.

realm.content:
## Recados en Eldmark

In Eldmark, **el heraldo** carries the news. Today's news keeps its tense: **el rey dice que la puerta está cerrada**. Yesterday's prophecy steps back: «El dragón despertará» → **el oráculo dijo que el dragón despertaría**. And a quest giver who says «Volved mañana» **os pide que volváis mañana**.

vocabulary.example: El heraldo dice que los orcos están en Frostmarch.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The herald says the orcs are in Frostmarch.

vocabulary.example: La elfa nos contó que el Bosque Umbrío estaba lleno de lobos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The elf told us the Bosque Umbrío was full of wolves.

vocabulary.example: El enano me preguntó si tenía una montura.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The dwarf asked me whether I had a mount.

vocabulary.example: El mago aseguró que el hechizo funcionaría.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mage assured us the spell would work.

vocabulary.example: El paladín dijo que saldría hacia Deepanvil al día siguiente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The paladin said he would leave for Deepanvil the next day.

vocabulary.example: Dijo que el botín estaba allí, en la mazmorra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He said the loot was there, in the dungeon.

vocabulary.example: El heraldo grita las noticias en la plaza de Highgate.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The herald shouts the news in Highgate's square.

vocabulary.example: El oráculo dijo que el invierno sería largo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The oracle said the winter would be long.

vocabulary.example: El pergamino dice que la llave está en Emberhold.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The scroll says the key is in Emberhold.

bites.title: Messages in Eldmark
bites.rule: The herald passes on today's news in the same tense (dice que está). Yesterday's prophecy steps back, so está becomes estaba and será becomes sería.
bites.example: El oráculo dijo que el dragón despertaría.
bites.example_meaning: The oracle said the dragon would wake up.

listening.text: La maga dijo que tenía frío.
listening.meaning: The mage said she was cold.

listening.text: Nos pide que llevemos una antorcha.
listening.meaning: She's asking us to bring a torch.
listening.note: New word: la antorcha = the torch.

listening.text: El heraldo dice que el rey está enfermo.
listening.meaning: The herald says the king is ill.

listening.text: El enano aseguró que volvería con el botín.
listening.meaning: The dwarf assured us he would come back with the loot.

listening.text: El oráculo contó que el dragón dormía allí.
listening.meaning: The oracle told us the dragon slept there.
listening.note: New word: el oráculo = the oracle.

builds.text: El heraldo dice que la puerta está cerrada.
builds.meaning: The herald says the gate is closed.

builds.text: La elfa dijo que vendría al día siguiente.
builds.meaning: The elf said she would come the next day.

spots.sentence: Ayer el mago dijo que el hechizo funcionará, pero falló.
spots.why: After dijo que the future becomes the conditional.

spots.sentence: El enano me preguntó sí tenía una montura.

sorts.title: The herald reports: dijo que…
sorts.why: After dijo que the present becomes the imperfect and the future the conditional.

quiz.prompt: El oráculo: «El dragón duerme.» → Ayer el oráculo dijo que el dragón ___, pero hoy está despierto.
quiz.explanation: After dijo que the present steps back to the imperfect, so duerme becomes dormía. Today he's awake, so the present can't stay.
hints: Dijo is past and the fact is no longer true.

quiz.prompt: El enano: «¿Tienes una montura?» → El enano me preguntó ___ tenía una montura.
quiz.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with preguntar si, and this si has no accent.
hints: There is no question word to keep, so use whether.

conversations.title: The missed council
conversations.scenario: Torvak the dwarf missed the council in Highgate; Brenna the paladin tells him what was said.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Torvak, ¿dónde estabas? Te perdiste el consejo.
lines.meaning: Torvak, where were you? You missed the council.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Estaba en la mazmorra. ¿Qué dijo el rey?
lines.meaning: I was in the dungeon. What did the king say?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Dijo que los orcos estaban cerca de Frostmarch.
lines.meaning: He said the orcs were near Frostmarch.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Y nos preguntó si iríamos con él?
lines.meaning: And did he ask us whether we would go with him?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, y le contesté que estaríamos listos.
lines.meaning: Yes, and I answered that we would be ready.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Y la maga? ¿Qué comentó?
lines.meaning: And the mage? What did she say?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Comentó que su dragón tenía miedo de los orcos.
lines.meaning: She mentioned that her dragon was afraid of the orcs.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Ja! Dile que mi hacha no tiene miedo de nada.
lines.meaning: Ha! Tell her my axe isn't afraid of anything.

meadowbrook.content:
## Recados en la granja

In Meadowbrook news travels from the seed shop to the tavern. Today's news keeps its tense: **Rosa dice que las semillas llegan el lunes**. Last summer's news steps back: «Pescaré un pez enorme» → **Leo dijo que pescaría un pez enorme**. And the mayor **nos pide que vayamos al festival**.

vocabulary.example: Rosa dice que las fresas están muy dulces este año.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa says the strawberries are very sweet this year.

vocabulary.example: Leo nos contó que el río estaba helado en invierno.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo told us the river was frozen in winter.

vocabulary.example: Nora comentó que su vaca no quería salir del establo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora mentioned that her cow didn't want to leave the barn.

vocabulary.example: El alcalde nos pide que decoremos la plaza.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mayor is asking us to decorate the square.

vocabulary.example: Leo dijo que el día anterior pescó tres truchas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo said he caught three trout the day before.

vocabulary.example: Nora aseguró que la cosecha sería buena.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora assured us the harvest would be good.

vocabulary.example: El tablón de anuncios dice que el festival es el sábado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The notice board says the festival is on Saturday.

vocabulary.example: Leo me contó que la trucha más grande vive bajo el puente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo told me the biggest trout lives under the bridge.

bites.title: Village news
bites.rule: Rosa's news today keeps its tense (dice que llegan). Last season's news steps back, so llegan becomes llegaban and pescaré becomes pescaría.
bites.example: Leo dijo que pescaría un pez enorme.
bites.example_meaning: Leo said he would catch a huge fish.

listening.text: Rosa nos pide que plantemos maíz.
listening.meaning: Rosa is asking us to plant maize.

listening.text: Rosa dice que la tienda abre tarde.
listening.meaning: Rosa says the shop opens late.

listening.text: Leo contó que pescó una trucha enorme.
listening.meaning: Leo told us he caught a huge trout.
listening.note: New word: la trucha = the trout.

listening.text: Nora dijo que la cosecha era excelente.
listening.meaning: Nora said the harvest was excellent.
listening.note: New word: la cosecha = the harvest.

listening.text: El alcalde aseguró que el festival sería precioso.
listening.meaning: The mayor assured us the festival would be lovely.

builds.text: Rosa dice que las semillas llegan el lunes.
builds.meaning: Rosa says the seeds arrive on Monday.

builds.text: Leo dijo que pescaría un pez enorme.
builds.meaning: Leo said he would catch a huge fish.

spots.sentence: Ayer Nora dijo que su vaca tiene fiebre, pero hoy ya está bien.
spots.why: After dijo que the present steps back; the fever is over, so it can't stay.

spots.sentence: El alcalde nos pide que decoramos la plaza.

sorts.title: Leo said… which tense after dijo que?
sorts.why: The present becomes the imperfect, the future becomes the conditional and the preterite stays.

quiz.prompt: Rosa: «Las semillas llegan el lunes.» → Rosa dice que las semillas ___ (llegar) el lunes.
quiz.explanation: With dice que (present) the tense stays: llegan.
hints: A present reporting verb keeps the same tense.

quiz.prompt: El alcalde: «Decorad la plaza.» → El alcalde nos pide que ___ la plaza.
quiz.explanation: A request after pide que takes the present subjunctive, and vosotros becomes nosotros: decoremos.
hints: A request, not a fact.
He's asking us: nosotros.

rustwake.content:
## Mensajes en el páramo

On the wasteland every message comes through **el radiorreloj**. Live news keeps its tense: **Marta dice que el agua filtrada cuesta diez tuercas**. Yesterday's broadcast steps back: «Habrá una tormenta de ceniza» → **la radio dijo que habría una tormenta de ceniza**. And **el capataz Ruiz nos pide que volvamos a la cúpula**.

vocabulary.example: Marta dice que la gaseosa Zafiro está fría.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta says the Zafiro soda is cold.

vocabulary.example: El capataz Ruiz explicó que la antena no funcionaba.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Foreman Ruiz explained that the antenna wasn't working.

vocabulary.example: Leo el buscador me aseguró que encontraría más tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo the scavenger assured me he would find more nuts.

vocabulary.example: El robot jardinero me preguntó si quería tomates.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The gardener robot asked me whether I wanted tomatoes.

vocabulary.example: Leo contó que ese día vio un escarabajo gigante.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo told us he saw a giant beetle that day.

vocabulary.example: Leo dijo que la gasolinera estaba vacía y que no había nadie allí.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo said the petrol station was empty and there was nobody there.

vocabulary.example: El radiorreloj dice que la señal es débil.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The wrist radio says the signal is weak.

vocabulary.example: El aviso decía que había radiación cerca del mercado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The warning said there was radiation near the market.

bites.title: Radio messages
bites.rule: Live from the radiorreloj: same tense (dice que hay polvo). Yesterday's broadcast steps back, so hay becomes había and habrá becomes habría.
bites.example: La radio dijo que habría una tormenta de ceniza.
bites.example_meaning: The radio said there would be an ash storm.

listening.text: Marta dice que el tónico es caro.
listening.meaning: Marta says the tonic is expensive.

listening.text: Ruiz nos pide que reparemos la antena.
listening.meaning: Ruiz is asking us to repair the antenna.

listening.text: El capataz dijo que la cúpula estaba cerrada.
listening.meaning: The foreman said the Dome was closed.

listening.text: La radio anunció que el polvo llegaría pronto.
listening.meaning: The radio announced that the dust would arrive soon.

listening.text: Leo explicó que la señal era muy débil.
listening.meaning: Leo explained that the signal was very weak.
listening.note: New word: la señal = the signal.

builds.text: Marta dice que el agua filtrada cuesta diez tuercas.
builds.meaning: Marta says filtered water costs ten nuts.

builds.text: La radio dijo que habría una tormenta.
builds.meaning: The radio said there would be a storm.

spots.sentence: Ayer Leo me aseguró que encontrará tuercas, pero volvió sin nada.
spots.why: After a past verb the future becomes the conditional.

spots.sentence: El capataz Ruiz nos pide que volvemos a la cúpula.

sorts.title: A report or an order?

items.text: Ruiz dice que la cúpula está cerrada.
Ruiz nos dice que cerremos la puerta.
Marta dice que no tiene agua.
Marta nos pide que traigamos tuercas.
La radio dice que hay polvo.
Leo me dice que escuche la radio.

sorts.why: Passing on a fact takes the indicative; telling someone to do something takes the present subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: La radio: «Habrá una tormenta de ceniza.» → Ayer la radio dijo que ___ una tormenta de ceniza, y llegó por la noche.
quiz.explanation: After dijo que the future steps back to the conditional, so habrá becomes habría.
hints: After a past verb, the future becomes the conditional.

quiz.prompt: Ruiz: «Volved a la cúpula.» → Ruiz nos dice que ___ (volver) a la cúpula.
quiz.explanation: An order reported with dice que takes the present subjunctive; vosotros becomes nosotros: volvamos.
hints: An order takes the subjunctive.
Volver keeps its o (no ue) in the nosotros form.
